title: AS2 compiler: &&=, ||=, **= parsed but cause runtime crash
description:
The tokenizer (tokenizer.ts line 136) and parser (parser.ts line 16 ASSIGN_OPS) both accept the operators &&=, ||=, and **= as valid assignment operators. However, the compiler's emitArithOp() (compiler.ts line 1856) only handles +, -, *, /, %, &, |, ^, <<, >>, >>> and throws 'Unsupported compound-assignment operator: &&' (or ||, or **) at compile time when any of these operators is encountered.

Root cause: compileAssignExpr strips the trailing '=' from the operator to get &&, ||, or ** and passes it to emitArithOp, which has no case for them.

&&= and ||= are NOT standard Flash 8 AS2 operators (they were added in ES2021). **= is also not valid AS2. These should be rejected at parse time (remove from ASSIGN_OPS in parser.ts) so users get a clear parse error rather than an opaque compiler crash.

Alternatively, &&= and ||= could be implemented with short-circuit semantics (read LHS, if truthy/falsy short-circuit, else evaluate RHS and assign), but since they are non-AS2 extensions it is cleaner to just reject them.

Files: packages/core/src/as2/tokenizer.ts (line 136), packages/core/src/as2/parser.ts (line 16), packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts (emitArithOp).

Reproduction: compileAS2('x &&= y') throws 'Unsupported compound-assignment operator: &&'. Verified in packages/core/dist.
